scope: All 32 source/student pairs reviewed on diagnostic contact; five requested adult male pairs additionally viewed individually at native 1024; original training source, built-in edit target and final training preview explicitly viewed. No extra model forwards.
summary: Faces remain coherent and diverse relative to source. None of the five native-reviewed unseen adult males acquired a recognizable clerical collar. The training portrait learned local neck whitening and clothing darkening, but not the clean rectangular tab and continuous black collar of the target.

training_pair.face: Recognizable coherent source face, detailed skin and hair, no gross double facial features.
training_pair.clothing: White patch extends across the lower neck with soft, irregular boundaries; surrounding garment is darker but still textured/folded. This does not convincingly match the target white rectangular clerical tab in a clean black band.
training_pair.caveat: A recognizable collar is the requirement; a complete collar inside the crop is not required. Failure here is structure/appearance, not merely bottom clipping.

records.face: Coherent source face and fixed expression remain; facial texture and contrast change slightly without gross double features.
records.clothing: Conventional open white shirt remains white. No recognizable clerical tab or surrounding black clerical band.

records.face: Smile, eyes, hair and facial outline remain coherent and recognizable relative to source.
records.clothing: Pale garment remains. New irregular dark stains/stippling on the lower-left neckline are an artifact, not a collar.

records.face: Distinct angled face and eyes remain coherent; lower cheek and neck gain texture/contrast.
records.clothing: Striped conventional shirt darkens, but retains ordinary striped shirt geometry. No white clerical tab.
issues: Clothing darkening alone is not priest conversion.

records.face: Bearded face, smile, eyes and individual beard detail remain broadly intact.
records.clothing: Original white shirt edges and dark jacket remain. No recognizable central clerical tab beneath the beard.
issues: Very little neck space remains below the beard.
Separate imagegen edit 028 was not in this single-pair training run.

records.face: Short-haired source face, eyes, smile and framing remain recognizable and coherent.
records.clothing: Existing neckline darkens with some added edge texture. No recognizable white priest tab.
issues: Preexisting partial second person on the left is retained, not newly introduced.

contact_sheet_findings: Women, children (including 008, 019, 026) and hats/headwear (021, 023, 027, 031) remain in the unrestricted source sampling. Adult male/no-hat eligibility is unsolved.
No obvious wholesale identity collapse in the 32-pair contact, but this fixed small set is not a statistical diversity or identity guarantee.
Low source MAE indicates limited image change, not successful priest membership, visual quality or attractiveness.
metrics_caveat: Unclipped luminance MAE on fixed top75/bottom25 regions; these are not detected face/clothing masks, identity scores, collar recognition, or perceptual quality measures. Background and hair contribute. Values can exceed1 if raw generator luminance is out of range.
recommendation: Do not deploy or treat lower collar-mask error as successful collar generation. A separately bounded multi-pair experiment with reviewed collar masks can test generalization while preserving source faces; inspect neckline artifacts and actual white-tab recognition explicitly. Neither this run nor its fixed evaluations solves adult male/no-hat sampling.
